newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa futures climb back as pound weakens.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa futures climb back as pound weakens.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures climbed back from the day's lows to end Monday steadier mostly on currency factors, traders said.
The market fell more than anticipated this morning, with benchmark March falling by 11 stg against trade expectations of two stg lower.
But it rallied quite quickly in the afternoon when New York opened a bit stronger than expected and prices then drifted in a narrow band for the rest of the day.
By the close, the benchmark contract was unchanged at 896 stg a tonne after ranging between 885 and 897.
There was no fundamental news and traders said the dominant factor remained sterling which was slightly weaker against the dollar in European trading.
Volume was a modest 3,580 lots, centered on March position.
European fourth quarter 1996 cocoa grind data, a key barometer of cocoa demand, is due to be released this week. This will be followed by U.S. data on January 17.
Traders expect the European data to show an increase or fall of five percent.
"Anything outside this level may trigger some movement in prices," said one.

A Reuters poll showed that while cocoa demand in Europe continues healthy, growth in origin processing and a pick-up in grindings at the end of 1995 would leave the 1996 fourth quarter grind struggling to break even.
Analysts estimate the Dutch grind to have risen by five percent higher year-on-year, UK down by 10 percent on closure of one of Mars plants and German off by some two percent.

In other news, some Nigerian cocoa traders in the state on Ondo, which produces two-thirds of Nigeria's cocoa, have protested to the authorities over the imposition of taxes by members of a state agency.
